contexts.text: A multitude dry of thirst () = penury of Knowledges of spiritual things.
Here drought is treated of, or no good and truth.
A torrid and dry life.

I called a drought upon the land (); here a drought = a lack of dew and rain, thus a lack of truth from any good; a drought upon the com = the lack of good; and a drought upon the new wine = a lack of truth.
To set as a land of dryness () = to extinguish all truth.
A drought upon the waters that they may be dried up () = that there is no life in truths, from falsification. AC 8869:4.
He made the sea for dryness () = the dissipation of falsity.
By the ephah and the homer dry things were measured.
A drought upon the waters = the deprivation and consumption of the truths of faith.
The ground is said to be broken up, from drought; thus from a lack of truth from Heaven.
That there is such an endeavour in its dry things also...
O how dry is the joy of Heaven!
Man (without woman) is dry, etc.
I saw the dry fire of a hearth...
A drought that they may be dried up = vastation. That drought, and drying up = where there is no truth. References.

That the Church will be established with them, is signified by I will make the wilderness a pool of waters, and a dry land into a spring of waters (). It is called a wilderness when there is not yet any good because there is not yet any truth; from which the land is also called dry.
A drought upon the waters that they may dry up = no longer any truths. AE 587:10. ( = the desolation of truth. AE 355:17.)
The year of drought () = a state of the loss and deprivation of truth.
A dry land () = where there is no truth, and thence no good.
A land of solitude and of drought () = here, as elsewhere in the Word, a state of no perception of good.
A dry place like a wilderness () = the falsities of doctrine... Drought in the threshold () = the total desolation of truth.
He maketh the outlets of the waters into dryness ()... Waters = truths; dryness, the deprivation of them from no light and affection.

I will make the wilderness a pool of waters, and the dry land into springs of waters = to infill the spiritual man and the natural man with truths, where before there were no truths; the spiritual man in which there are no truths is meant by the wilderness... and the natural man in which there are no truths is meant by the dry land, because before there was no influx of the Spiritual into it.
A land of drought and of dense shade () = the perception of good, and the understanding of truth bedimmed.
The dry places through which the evil Spirit wanders seeking rest = the states of evil and falsity which are of his life.
A land of droughts () = a state devoid of truths.
Man then puts off all senile severity, sadness, and dryness.
